verdicts.trueWording: Nine sentences; mean 14.11 words, population SD 4.43, range 5-21.
verdicts.note: Recomputed from the live PDF (HTTP 200, browser UA, pdftotext -enc UTF-8). The DM read-aloud box in the Introduction gives exactly 9 sentences, 127 words, mean 14.1111, population SD 4.4333, shortest 5, longest 21 - every figure reproduces. No quote supplied, so graded on substance not verbatim. LOCATOR CORRECTION: the passage is on printed p. 3 (PDF page 3, footer '3'), not p. 2; p. 2 is the Contents page.

verdicts.trueWording: Zero em dashes; zero contractions; one hyphen only.
verdicts.note: Recomputed from the live PDF: em-dash count 0, en-dash count 0, and a contraction scan returns an empty set. The passage's only intraword punctuation is the single hyphen in the compound modifier before 'iron'. No quote supplied, so graded on substance. Locator: printed p. 3, not p. 2.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: the verb enumeration presented as complete - it omits the finite verb 'takes' in sentence 1, so the passage carries eleven finite verbs, not the ten listed
verdicts.trueWording: No finite 'to be'; but sentence one also inflects 'takes'.
verdicts.note: The quotation appears word for word on printed p. 3. The primary limb is CONFIRMED: a scan for is/are/was/were/be/been/being/am over the passage returns an empty set. The enumeration limb fails. Sentence 1 is compound - one clause has the road as subject with the finite verb 'takes', the other has Castle Ravenloft with 'towers'. The claim's list keeps only the second. Every other listed verb checks out (keep, look, gapes, spans, creak, stare, grin, hangs, stand), and the participles passing/disappearing/leading/straining/spilling are correctly excluded. Locator: printed p. 3, not p. 2.

Quotation appears word for word in the DM read-aloud box, and every limb holds. Two second-person tokens across 127 words = 15.7480 per 1,000, which rounds to the claimed 15.75; they fall in sentence 1 and sentence 7, i.e. 2 of 9 sentences. Locator: printed p. 3 (PDF page 3), not p. 2.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'describes environments only as numeric thresholds' - the section's own figures refute 'only', since 55.56 percent of its sentences carry no digit and two of its ten subsections (Heavy Precipitation and Strong Wind) contain no numeral at all
verdicts.trueWording: When the temperature is 0 degrees Fahrenheit or lower
verdicts.note: Quotation verbatim on p. 195 (PDF page 195, footer matches). Both measurements reproduce EXACTLY: the section body with subheadings stripped is 512 words in 27 sentences; 12 of those 27 sentences contain a digit = 44.44 percent; and a digit-run count returns 23 numerals = 44.9219 per 1,000 words, matching 44.92 to the stated precision. I recovered the finder's tokenizer: plain digit runs, which split 10,000 into two and 3d10 into two. The characterisation limb is what fails - qualitative sentences such as the ones defining Difficult Terrain and the effect on open flames describe environments with no numeric threshold whatever.

verdicts.trueWording: Planes appendix 0.00; Environmental Effects 44.92 numerals per 1,000 words.
verdicts.note: Both endpoints independently confirmed from the two live PDFs. SRD 5.1 Appendix PH-C (The Planes of Existence, pp. 363-365) contains ZERO digits across 1,530 words of body prose once running heads and folios are stripped, giving 0.00 per 1,000. SRD 5.2.1 Environmental Effects gives 44.92 per 1,000 as at index 1042. 'Deleted' also holds: SRD 5.2.1 has no Planes of Existence appendix (string count 0) and no pantheon lore whatever (Egyptian, Norse, Celtic, Olympus all count 0); the plane names survive only inside spell and rules text. One wording caveat, not a limb failure: a 'factor' is undefined against a zero denominator, so the separation is absolute rather than multiplicative. No quote supplied, so graded on substance.

verdicts.trueWording: No second-person pronoun, no em dash, across 27 sentences.
verdicts.note: Recomputed from the live PDF. A you/your/yours/yourself/yourselves scan over the p. 195 body returns an empty set; em-dash count 0 and en-dash count 0; the sentence count is 27, matching. verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'in 5 paragraphs' - the prose sets 8 paragraphs, not 5; 5 counts blank-line blocks (the intro plus one per pantheon), but three of those blocks open a second paragraph with the SRD's first-line indent (the Egyptian, Celtic and Norse continuations)
verdicts.note: Heading verbatim on p. 360 (PDF page 360, footer matches); the extracted text carries soft-hyphen artifacts inside 'Fantasy-Historical' that render as the claimed string. The other limbs hold exactly: 550 words on a whitespace tokenizer, 22 sentences, four pantheons (Celtic, Egyptian, Greek, Norse). 'The only institutional prose in either SRD' survives adversarial checking - SRD 5.1's other two appendices are PH-A (Conditions, pure rules) and PH-C (Planes, places rather than institutions), and SRD 5.2.1 carries no lore prose at all, its two lowercase 'pantheon' hits being spell text for Divine Intervention and the spiritual guardian. The paragraph count is the one limb that fails. I found the indent markers directly in the extraction: three continuation paragraphs beyond the five blocks.

verdicts.trueWording: Mean 25.00 words, population SD 12.00, longest sentence 54.
verdicts.note: Recomputed from the live PDF and matching to four decimals: 550 words over 22 sentences gives mean 25.0000, population SD 12.0038, longest 54. Reproducing this required recovering the finder's tokenizer - whitespace splitting, which keeps em-dash-joined pairs and the non-breaking-hyphen compounds as single tokens. An alphanumeric tokenizer instead yields 556 words, mean 25.27, SD 12.22, longest 55; the claim is exact under the stated pdftotext route. No quote supplied, so graded on substance.

verdicts.trueWording: 27.27 percent against 11.11 percent of sentences over thirty words.
verdicts.note: Both halves reproduce exactly. Pantheon prose (p. 360): 6 of 22 sentences exceed 30 words = 27.27 percent. Planes appendix PH-C (pp. 363-365): 8 of 72 sentences exceed 30 words = 11.1111 percent. The 72 is reached by excluding the two bold run-in heads that a naive splitter counts as one-word sentences; counting them gives 74 and 10.81 percent, so the claim's figure identifies the correct basis. No quote supplied, so graded on substance.

verdicts.trueWording: Where the land plummets from the snowy hills
verdicts.note: Quotation appears word for word as the opening of The Norse Pantheon on p. 360, and both limbs hold. The entry opens on three stacked place clauses - the land and hills, the longboats and beach, the glaciers - before it reaches its main clause naming the land of the Vikings and the pantheon's home; no deity is named anywhere in that opening paragraph. The people is introduced through the climate that shapes it, which is the 'describes a people by its landscape' limb.

verdicts.trueWording: It will not, however, include lore references.
verdicts.note: Fetched live at HTTP 200 with a browser UA; the body is present in the served HTML, no summarizer involved. Quotation verbatim, byline 'by DND Staff May 6, 2024' matches the source attribution. The interval limb holds: the post is dated 6 May 2024 and SRD 5.2 was released 22 April 2025, an interval of 11 months 16 days, which 'a year before release' rounds fairly. Worth recording for the merger that the page itself forecasts release only as being within weeks of the Feb 2025 Monster Manual, so the page alone dates the lead at roughly nine to ten months; the full year comes from the actual release date.

verdicts.trueWording: DMsGuild is the place for you
verdicts.note: Fetched live at HTTP 200 with a browser UA; body present in the served HTML. The claim's quoted fragment appears word for word and continues to name DMsGuild. The 'rather than to the SRD' limb is supported by immediate context, not inference: the DMsGuild sentence follows directly on the sentence excluding lore references from SRD 5.2, in the same answer to the question of what SRD 5.2 will contain, so the post is explicitly routing setting-based creation away from the SRD.
